class.name: NetwSessionHandle
class.brief_description: The session plane of one session, gathered onto one object.
class.description: A client over the [code]session_*[/code], [code]participant_*[/code], [code]peer_*[/code] and [code]stats_*[/code] families on [NetwMultiplayer], reached as [method Netw.session] from any [Node]. Every member forwards to a flat verb, and the flat verb is the stable spelling: this repository's own suites, examples and browser call [NetwMultiplayer] directly, and a game reaches for this when it would rather hold the plane as one object. [codeblock] var s := Netw.session(self) s.entered.connect(on_entered) s.disconnected.connect(on_over) s.ended.connect(on_over) for participant: NetwParticipant in s.participants: scoreboard.add(participant) [/codeblock] [b]What this object buys over the flat surface is its signals.[/b] [Netw] is static and a static class publishes none, so a game that wants to hear a session's edges has to name the session to hear them. This object is where they are named once: [signal entered], [signal ended], [signal disconnected], [signal disconnecting], [signal participant_joined], [signal local_joined], [signal participant_left], [signal join_failed], [signal scene_live] and [signal presentation_changed], all relayed from the session that created it. One handle exists per session for the life of that session, so a game may hold it across an await. [signal disconnected] is the one member that relays a signal this framework does not own. [signal MultiplayerAPI.server_disconnected] is Godot's and stays reachable on [code]multiplayer[/code]; it is re-emitted here so one object returns every cause a session has to end, which is what a game pairing it with [signal ended] under one handler actually wants. Bringing a session UP is not on this object. A session comes online the ordinary Godot way, by assigning a [MultiplayerPeer] to [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer], the connect plane is [NetwConnectHandle] reached as [method Netw.connection], and joining is [method Netw.join], which routes prepare against submit off session state. This object is what a session already up admits, reports, and tears down.

method.name: activate_scene
method.description: Brings [param destination] up if it is not already live and returns the [NetwSceneHandle] it settled on, [code]null[/code] when nothing could be activated. [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_activate] holds the law, including which kinds of [param destination] are rejected and why; what differs here is the result, which is the view a caller goes on to use rather than the container node it would have to resolve one from. This verb is on the session rather than on a scene view because a recipe names no live scene yet, so there is no view to call it on. A scene already live is reached by [method Netw.scene]. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: bucket_of
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_bucket]: the per-peer bucket of [param type] that [param peer] carries, [code]null[/code] when it carries none.

method.name: kick
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.participant_kick]: ends [param participant]'s membership and turns their peer away carrying [param reason], which holds the law and the errors. This ends a membership rather than closing a connection, and [method leave] is how a peer ends its own. The local server's participant is refused here for that reason. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: leave
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.session_leave]: leaves the session this handle was created by, returning the promise that resolves once the peer is down.

method.name: participant_of
method.description: The [NetwParticipant] this session holds for [param peer], [code]null[/code] when it holds none. Forwards to [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_participant], which is the same result under the flat spelling.

method.name: present
method.description:
Names the scene this peer looks at, and [code]null[/code] names none. A local rendering choice and nothing else. It grants no viewership, sends nothing, and changes what no other peer sees, so a client presenting a scene it was never given still receives nothing of it. [method NetwSceneHandle.watch] is the verb that decides what reaches a participant. The framework never chooses for the game. A session presents nothing until something names a scene, and the scene it presents retiring clears the choice without taking another, so a peer between worlds draws nothing rather than whatever is left standing. [codeblock] func _on_scene_live(arena: NetwSceneHandle) -> void: Netw.session(self).present(arena) [/codeblock] That reads a scene going live as the scene to draw, which holds only while one world is live at a time. A game running several at once presents the world its own player stands in, or the last world any peer brought up takes the view from whoever was watching another. [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: if not is_multiplayer_authority(): return entity.reparented.connect(present_own_scene) present_own_scene()
func present_own_scene() -> void: Netw.session(self).present(entity.scene) [/codeblock] On a listen server this is what [HostSceneView] draws, because only a host runs scenes in worlds of their own. Several bodies in the presented scene each hear [signal NetwEntity.view_activated], and the camera is adopted automatically only where exactly one of them is local. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK this peer now presents that scene, or none ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE this session holds no live scene by that handle ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED this handle outlived its session [/codeblock]

method.name: request_scene
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_request]: asks server authority for the scene at [param path] over [param scope], one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.SceneChange], returning the promise that resolves when the scene is live or rejects when authority declines. A scene already live is reached by [method Netw.scene] and read through its own [NetwSceneHandle]; this verb is the asking. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: set_server_info
method.description: [method NetwMultiplayer.session_set_server_info]: replaces what this session advertises about itself, at runtime, so a name a player typed reaches the listing rather than the snapshot the session started from. [b]Server Only.[/b]

members.member: The [NetwAuthFlow] this session authenticates with, [code]null[/code] when it authenticates with none. [member NetwMultiplayer.auth_flow] under the flat spelling.

A [NetwSessionConfig] SNAPSHOT of what this session was configured with. Each read creates a new one and writing to it changes nothing, which is [method NetwMultiplayer.session_get_config]'s own contract: the live edits are [method Netw.configure_session] before the session comes up and [method set_server_info] after.
Whether this peer is a client of a session hosted elsewhere, so a listen-server host reads [code]false[/code] here. [member NetwMultiplayer.is_local_client].
Whether this session has a peer assigned and connected. [member NetwMultiplayer.is_online].
The [NetwParticipant] this session holds for this peer, [code]null[/code] before the local join is accepted. [signal local_joined] is the edge that fills it.
The scene [method present] last named, [code]null[/code] while this peer presents none. [method NetwMultiplayer.scene_presented].

Every [NetwParticipant] that has joined, including rows whose peer has since gone, which is what [member NetwMultiplayer.participants] returns and is the roster a scoreboard wants. The rows still CONNECTED are [member NetwMultiplayer.connected_participants].
What this peer is in the session, one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.Role]. [member NetwMultiplayer.role].
The [Node] this session's replicated branch hangs under, [code]null[/code] when the session is not mounted. [member NetwMultiplayer.root].

Every live scene, as the [NetwSceneHandle] each one is read through. The session keys its rows by an internal handle, and that handle never crosses onto this view: a caller naming one scene reaches for [method Netw.scene] instead.
[method NetwMultiplayer.stats_snapshot]: every counter this session keeps, keyed by the [enum NetwMultiplayer.Stat] constant that names it.

signal.name: disconnected
signal.description: Relayed from [signal MultiplayerAPI.server_disconnected]: the server this peer was connected to is gone, without having said so first. Godot's own signal, re-emitted here so one object returns every cause a session has to end. [signal ended] is the same event when this peer's own session tore down, and [signal disconnecting] is the host announcing it in advance.

signal.name: disconnecting
signal.description: The server has announced that it is going down, carrying [param reason]. [signal disconnected] is what arrives when it does not announce.

signal.name: ended
signal.description: This session has torn down. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_ended].

signal.name: entered
signal.description: This peer's join was accepted and the session is live for it. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_entered].

signal.name: join_failed
signal.description: This peer's own join was turned down, carrying the [param code] and the [param reason] the server gave. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.session_join_failed]. No membership was created, so [member local_participant] is still [code]null[/code] and [signal local_joined] never fires for that attempt. [method Netw.join]'s promise reports only that the request went out, so this is where a refusal arrives.

signal.name: local_joined
signal.description: The [NetwParticipant] the session holds for THIS peer has joined, which is also when [member local_participant] starts returning. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.participant_local_joined].

signal.name: presentation_changed
signal.description: The scene this peer presents has changed, carrying the handle left and the one taken, either of which may be [code]null[/code]. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.scene_presentation_changed]. Spent on a change and never on a repeat, so presenting the scene already presented announces nothing. A scene retiring clears the choice and announces that, naming [code]null[/code] as the destination rather than picking another scene.

signal.name: participant_joined
signal.description: A [NetwParticipant] has joined, this peer's own row included. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.participant_joined].

signal.name: participant_left
signal.description: A [NetwParticipant]'s membership has ended, whether their peer disconnected or [method kick] ended it. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.participant_left], which carries the ordering. [member NetwParticipant.is_active] already reads [code]false[/code] here, so this is the last edge at which a game can read the handle it filed that player under and erase its own row for them.

signal.name: scene_live
signal.description: A scene is live and reachable, carrying the [NetwSceneHandle] it is read through. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.scene_live]. This is where a game puts what a scene needs, and the handle it is handed is the one to keep. Watching a participant, observing an edge, and reading the scene's entities are all members on it. [b]It fires from the scene root's own tree entry, so the root's children have not entered yet.[/b] Their [member Node.multiplayer] is [code]null[/code] and their [code]@onready[/code] fields are unset, while [method Node.get_node] still answers with the unmounted node, so a helper reaching one reads a null session deep inside itself rather than failing here. Work that touches the scene's contents waits for the root's own [signal Node.ready], which [method Node.is_node_ready] says whether it has already had. [codeblock] func _on_scene_live(arena: NetwSceneHandle) -> void: if not arena.root.is_node_ready(): await arena.root.ready arena.root.get_node(^"Spawns").arrange() [/codeblock]
